decisions.reason: The same message already establishes the footer as a shared website component. The dark page theme is independently represented by the source Requirement and does not change footer-specific state.
The landing-page visual direction already specifies a dark theme. Retaining that theme across website pages does not change this landing-page-specific state.
The website page-theme decision does not alter the selected HTML and Tailwind CSS build stack.
Retaining the dark website theme does not change landing-page copy, section ordering, or the How It Works sequence.
The shared dark-theme decision does not change the requirement that the landing page have responsive behavior.
The website page-theme decision does not change which hero text receives emphasis.
Retaining the dark theme does not alter the requirement for a landing-page sign-up button.
The source decision concerns website pages, while the admin shell remains a distinct interface supporting both light and dark modes. Its separate same-message scope refinement is already represented.
Responsive breakpoint guidance is addressed by a separate clause and an existing same-message Event; the page-theme modification does not change that guidance.
